text.p: Greek Orthodox Church officials on Wednesday accused Islamic religious officials in Jerusalem of violating an Israeli court order in a dispute over ownership of two rooms near the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.
Officials of the Islamic Religious Authority, known as the Waqf, have denied occupying the rooms claimed by the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate.
The Islamic officials said they were only renovating the al-Khanqa mosque, which is separated from the Patriarchate by a wall.

"The Khanqa mosque's people have ignored a police order and a court order issued last week to freeze the building because they have no permit to build in the area," Metropolitan Timothy of the Greek Orthodox Church told reporters.

The mosque's director, Sheikh Yacoub Rajabi, countered: "We're only renovating and we don't need Israel's permission to renovate. Israel has no right to intervene in the work of the Islamic Waqf anyway."

Reporters on a tour of the disputed site organised by the Israeli Government Press office saw that half of the area of two rooms claimed by the Patriarchate was taken over and two of the doors were sealed with bricks.

"Two weeks ago the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate wanted to open the rooms...we found the two rooms of the monastery had disappeared, been broken into and taken by the Khanqa mosque," said Metropolitan Christollophis of the Greek Orthodox Church.
"This was an infringement to the status quo and we immediately informed the Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority asking them to restore the status quo," he added.

On the other side of the wall, where Islamic Waqf workers were renovating al-Khanqa, Rajabi denied taking over the rooms near the church that stands on the traditional site of the crucifixion of Jesus.
"The wall you see right here is an ancient wall and what we have done is paint it," he told reporters who noticed fresh paint had been splashed on the dividing wall.
Metropolitan Timothy said the mosque officials were building toilets over the church's roof. Rajabi showed reporters the toilets and said they were being built on a rooftop belonging to the mosque.
Israel and the Palestinian Authority have tried to resolve the dispute. Patriarchate officials met last week with Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to seek his help.

Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem, including the walled Old City, in the 1967 Middle East war and regards all of Jerusalem as its capital. The PLO wants East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
